Memory.value: I cannot tell a clear story of what happened even to myself
When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event.
I can taste what I tasted during the event when the memory returns

Negative Appraisals.value: Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy

vignette: Kai had always been a meticulous person, with a keen eye for detail and a passion for numbers. As a financial analyst, they took pride in their ability to make sense of complex data and provide clarity to their clients. But that was before the night that shattered their world. It started with a knock on the door. Kai's partner, who had passed away a few years prior, was not there to answer it. Alone in the house, Kai opened the door to find two strangers standing on their porch. What happened next is still a jumbled mess of sounds and images in Kai's mind. They recall feeling a sense of unease as one of the men pushed his way into the house, but the specifics of what followed are hazy. Kai remembers hearing footsteps, heavy breathing, and muffled voices. They remember the taste of fear - metallic and bitter - which still lingers on their tongue whenever memories of that night resurface. In the aftermath, Kai struggled to piece together a coherent narrative of the event. Their mind felt foggy, as if trying to recall the details was like grasping at wisps of smoke. The more they tried to remember, the more elusive the memories became. It wasn't until months later, when sounds from that night began echoing in their head - creaks and groans that transported them back to that moment - that Kai realized the full extent of what had happened. As a result, Kai's world shrunk. They stopped going out, avoiding public places where they might encounter people misbehaving or authority figures like police officers, who seemed to embody a sense of powerlessness. Simple tasks became daunting challenges. When colleagues offered constructive criticism at work, Kai felt a wave of anxiety wash over them. It wasn't just the words themselves but the tone - dismissive and condescending - that sent them spiraling back into the darkness. Kai began to doubt their own abilities. "What if I'm losing my mind?" they would ask themselves in quiet moments. The reactions they experienced since the event seemed irrational, uncontrollable, and utterly alien. They couldn't shake the feeling that they were teetering on the edge of sanity. As weeks turned into months, Kai's performance at work suffered. Colleagues noticed their mistakes, and clients began to lose confidence in their abilities. The sense of purpose that once drove them was dwindling, leaving behind a hollow shell of uncertainty. "Nothing feels meaningful anymore," Kai confided in a friend. It wasn't just the event itself but the aftermath - the inability to make sense of it all, to grasp control - that had drained life's color. When the local police department launched an initiative to increase community engagement, Kai felt their heart sink. The officers' friendly smiles and reassuring words only seemed like thinly veiled threats, reminding them of the night when they were left feeling so utterly helpless. It was then that Kai realized they couldn't keep going on like this - avoiding life, doubting themselves, and fearing the worst. As they sit in their dimly lit living room, surrounded by stacks of unopened mail and untouched financial reports, Kai finally acknowledges the weight of their burden. The event has left them feeling lost and disconnected from the world. They hope that seeking help will allow them to rebuild a sense of self, to rediscover meaning, and to quiet the cacophony of fears that have held them hostage for so long.
